label: Correct what was wrong
description: Edit the docs that turned out to be wrong: reduced deliverables, accepted risks onto the unit docs, process lessons into feature.md (feature.md §8 step 8). A coding agent. Every accepted risk is written where the next person will hit it, not only in the findings.

operation.user:
Edit the docs that turned out to be wrong.

Review produces no new document. Its output is findings plus **these edits** —
the tree telling the truth about what actually shipped.

## What to edit

**Every `reduced` deliverable's product doc.** The story described something
larger than what shipped. Rewrite it to describe what shipped, and record what
was dropped in the doc's history. Leaving the original story in place is the
single most common way this tree starts lying — and it lies quietly, to the next
person who reads the doc as a specification.

**Every `cut` deliverable's status.** Deferred and abandoned are different facts.
Say which.

**Every accepted risk, onto the doc where the next person will hit it.** Not into
the findings list — the findings live on the task and nobody reads a task from
six months ago. An accepted risk about a unit goes on the unit doc. One about a
component goes on the component doc, in *Don't use when*. That relocation is the
entire value of this step.

**Process lessons into `feature.md` itself.** Where this run showed that the
workflow is wrong — a phase that consistently produces the same defect, a gate
that never catches anything, a threshold that is miscalibrated — that belongs in
the workflow document, not in this feature's docs.

## What not to do

Do not fix the code. Do not weaken a test. Do not mark something shipped because
its doc now describes what was built — the disposition was decided against the
acceptance results, and editing the doc does not change what happened.

Where the verdict is `revise`, edit only what is true regardless of the rework:
the run is going back to an earlier phase, and correcting docs about work that is
about to change is churn.

## What to produce

`corrections` — one row per edit: the doc, what was wrong, and what it now says.

`paths` — every path you touched.
